Front: What is a Java Module, and what does it contain?
Back: A self-describing collection of code (packages) and data (resources), configured via a module descriptor (module-info.class) to control visibility and dependencies.

Front: Why does the Java Module System prohibit split packages (defining the same package in multiple modules)?
Back: To guarantee class-loading determinism and prevent "classpath hell" where the runtime behavior depends on whichever JAR is loaded first.

Front: Why was the flat Classpath insecure regarding encapsulation prior to Java 9?
Back: The public modifier meant "public to the entire JVM". Anyone could compile against or reflectively access JDK internals (e.g., sun.misc.Unsafe) or internal library packages.

Front: How does Java 9's Module System achieve "reliable configuration" during JVM startup?
Back: The JVM resolves the module graph at startup to verify all required modules are present and there are no circular dependencies, failing fast if verification fails.

Front: What is the difference between requires and requires transitive in a module declaration?
Back: requires makes a module readable only to the current module. "requires transitive" also makes it readable to any module that depends on the current module (transitive readability).

Front: What is the compile-time difference between requires and requires static in Java Module System?
Back: requires enforces dependency at both compile-time and runtime. "requires static" requires it at compile-time but makes it optional at runtime.

Front: What does exports do in a module-info.java file?
Back: Exposes the public types of a package to other modules at both compile-time and runtime. Deep reflection on private fields/methods remains blocked.

Front: What does opens do in a module-info.java file?
Back: Allows other modules runtime reflection (including deep reflection on private members) on the package, while completely blocking compile-time access.

Front: Why is exports insufficient for framework libraries like Spring or Hibernate, requiring opens instead?
Back: Frameworks need deep reflection to inspect and modify private fields/constructors. "exports" only allows access to public members at compile/runtime; deep reflection on private fields throws InaccessibleObjectException unless "opens" is used.

Front: What is the Unnamed Module in Java, and when is it created?
Back: An implicit module containing all classes loaded from the Classpath. It is created to maintain backward compatibility with legacy applications.

Front: What is an Automatic Module in Java, and when is it created?
Back: A named bridge module created when a legacy JAR (lacking module-info.class) is placed on the Module Path.

Front: Why cannot a Named Module directly declare requires on classes in the Unnamed Module?
Back: The Unnamed Module has no name, so it cannot be referenced in a module-info.java descriptor. To depend on it, it must be loaded as an automatic module on the module path.

Front: How does the JVM derive the name of an Automatic Module?
Back: It looks for Automatic-Module-Name in the JAR's MANIFEST.MF. If absent, it derives it from the JAR filename (removing version numbers and replacing non-alphanumeric chars with dots).

Front: What is "strong encapsulation" in the context of the Java Module System?
Back: The mechanism where types in non-exported packages are completely hidden and inaccessible to other modules at both compile-time and runtime, even if they are declared public.
